claim: App is the central owner of platform services, executors, entities, windows, observers, globals, and invalidation maps.
App construction captures foreground/background executors and asserts that construction occurs on the main thread.
Entity state is type-erased in EntityMap while strong handles use atomic reference counts stored behind Arc<RwLock>.
Updating an Entity temporarily leases its value out of EntityMap; re-entrant reads or updates of the same entity fail.
Entity handles are typed identifiers; state access requires an App context.
Context<T> is a mutable App wrapper plus a weak handle to the current entity.
Context::notify delegates to App::notify for the current EntityId.
During rendering, App records which entities each window accessed and maps those entities back to the window invalidator.
App::notify filters invalidation to windows that currently track the entity and invalidates the corresponding view.
WindowInvalidator records dirty views, coalesces the dirty transition, queues observer notification, and wakes the platform frame source.
Cached AnyView rendering reuses prepaint and paint ranges when bounds, mask, text style, and entity dirtiness permit.
Application::run delegates the event loop to Platform::run and invokes startup with a mutable App.
App::open_window allocates a Window, builds its root Entity, performs an initial draw, and stores the window.
Window installs a platform frame callback that draws dirty content, presents the Scene, completes the platform frame, and re-wakes when still dirty.
A Window draw performs root request_layout, prepaint including hit testing, then paint into the next frame.
Window::draw swaps next/rendered frames and Window::present passes the rendered Scene to PlatformWindow::draw.
Element defines three explicit phases: request_layout, prepaint, and paint.
Platform and PlatformWindow are broad interfaces covering lifecycle/services and window/input/render responsibilities respectively.

claim: PlatformWindow directly owns frame callbacks, input callbacks, drawing, atlas access, IME positioning, and many window controls.
notes: Static count: 77 PlatformWindow methods; see research report methodology.

Editor tests verify IME composition, clipping, undo grouping, and multi-cursor behavior.
Dropping a GPUI Task cancels it unless detached; foreground and background executors have distinct thread constraints.
GPUI timers use the scheduler clock, enabling virtual time and deterministic advance_clock/run_until_parked tests.
gpui_tokio owns or accepts a Tokio runtime and aborts Tokio work when the wrapping GPUI task is cancelled.
TestWindow can simulate platform input and frame requests and optionally render through a PlatformHeadlessRenderer.
TestAppContext drives actions, keystrokes, text input, and scheduler progress deterministically.
The element arena localizes unsafe allocation and invalidates ArenaBox handles when cleared.

ui_prompt depends on workspace settings and installs a product-specific prompt renderer into GPUI.

ZZZ startup initializes gpui_tokio and the application services inside Application::run.
ZZZ currently has view-level cache invalidation but no explicit public measure/arrange/paint invalidation categories.

Windows implements the GPUI accessibility bridge through accesskit_windows.
Wayland implements the GPUI accessibility bridge through accesskit_unix.

The gpui-kit facade re-exports GPUI and keeps application imports stable across GPUI dependency changes.
gpui-mobile depends on a pinned Zed gpui and gpui_wgpu revision rather than implementing a separate core.
iOS Platform::run delegates lifecycle ownership to UIApplicationMain and resumes through FFI callbacks.

Compile-fail diagnostics are exercised with trybuild UI fixtures.
Dynamic classes generate a runtime matcher with permissive warning/ignore behavior or strict-mode panic.
gpui-toolkit vendors Zed GPUI snapshots plus a documented local patch stack instead of providing an independent core lineage.

gpui-builder property tests compare independent solver forms and assert finite non-overallocating results.
gpui-builder has a warmed steady-state zero-allocation contract.
gpui-design is pure data by default; GPUI integration is an optional feature.
gpui-design separates shape/spacing/interaction/animation rules from color themes.
gpui-ui-kit maps component semantics into GPUI AccessKit roles but records cross-platform screen-reader QA as pending.
The UI kit also maintains a separate per-frame platform-neutral accessibility tree and deterministic snapshots.
gpui-profiler provides opt-in heap-allocation probes with exportable labeled samples.
The custom draw registry is backend-specific and stores process-local callbacks by opaque ID.
